title: Live imaging and quantitation of nascent transcription using the MS2/MCP system in the Drosophila embryo
protocol: On the morning of the experiment, change the fly cage plate to a fresh apple juice agar plate containing yeast paste and wait 1 h for flies to lay retained embryos.
After 1 hour, change the plate again.
Wash off the plate with NaCl (0.7%)/TritonX-100 (0.05%) solution.
Add freshly prepared 50% bleach to the plate for 2 min to dechorionate embryos.
Decant embryos into a sieve and wash them with water until free of bleach.
Dry the sieve with paper towels, removing excess water from embryos.
Cut a square from a fresh apple juice plate and place it on top of the plate so it is elevated.
Place the plate under a dissection microscope.
Transfer embryos onto the agar square using a brush.
Line up the embryos so that the area in which the gene of interest will be expressed is facing upwards.
Exclude embryos that have already entered late nuclear cycles or are gastrulating.
Prepare a cover slip/halocarbon oil bridge on a Lumox imaging dish.
Cut a pipette tip and add 70 μL of halocarbon oil (7:1, halocarbon oil 700:halocarbon oil 27) onto the middle of the imaging dish.
Place a coverslip on each side of the drop of oil to create a bridge.
Ensure that the two coverslips are approximately 0.6 cm apart.
Fix embryos in place with a heptane glue coated coverslip.
Gently drop the heptane glue coated coverslip onto the embryos, with the glue side facing down.
Press the coverslip onto the embryos using tweezers.
Place the coverslip with attached embryos onto the coverslip-bridge.
Secure the top coverslip in place with a dot of nail polish.
Set the scanning frequency of the resonant scan head to 8,000 Hz.
Configure the microscope for bidirectional scanning.
Acquire images at 8-bit resolution and 1,024 pixels per line with 700 lines.
Capture images with a pixel size of 378.79 nm × 378.79 nm and an image size of 387.5 μm × 264.77 μm.
Set the pixel dwell time to 1.04 μs.
Use a Leica TCS SP8 AOBS inverted confocal microscope with a resonant scan head and a 40×/ 1.3 HC PL apochromatic oil objective.
Collect images using hybrid detectors.
Excite fluorophores with a white laser set to 70% and specific wavelengths for different channels.
Acquire z-stacks continuously with 1 μm steps.
Ensure minimal photobleaching during imaging.
Adjust z-step size if the gene of interest is not highly expressed.
Find embryos on the imaging dish using brightfield illumination.
Rotate embryos to align their AP axis horizontally.
Check embryo age by examining nuclei under fluorescence illumination at 561 nm excitation line.
Select an embryo where nuclei have migrated to the surface and are undergoing nc13.
Set up a time lapse including the full depth of nuclei in the z-direction.
Extract fluorescent signal from each nucleus using the initial semi-automated data analysis pipeline.
Track the extracted signal over time within the dataset.
Combine data analysis using Imaris software 9.2 with open-access, custom python scripts.
Use sample time-lapse datasets provided for reference and practice.
Apply the analysis pipeline to different microscopes, magnifications, and embryo regions as needed.
Ensure the pipeline is user-friendly for those without coding knowledge or programming language familiarity.
Reimage developing Drosophila embryo over time using z-slices.
Analyze images in Imaris software.
Render images in 3D using Imaris.
Crop time-lapse dataset to a region of interest.
Segment nuclei using the “surfaces” module and His-RFP channel.
Use either absolute intensity or background subtraction thresholding for segmentation.
Track nuclei through time using an autoregressive motion algorithm.
Smooth detectable objects using a Gaussian filter set at 1 μm.
Identify transcription sites using the “spots” function with MCP-GFP channel.
Select “split touching objects” when choosing the “absolute intensity” thresholding option.
Define the seed point diameter as 3 μm for initial segmentation.
Choose 1.3 μm as the start value for “diameter of largest sphere which fits into object” in the background subtraction method.
Adjust the slider until nuclei are sufficiently identified and shaded without touching each other.
Select classifiers to separate nuclei by choosing appropriate filters such as Number of voxels, Position Z, Distance to image border XY, Quality and Area.
Track nuclei through time in 3D using the autoregressive motion algorithm.
Set the maximum frame gap size to 5.
Set the maximum travel distance to 5 μm.
Manually correct tracks and nuclei in the “edit” and “edit tracks” tabs.
Disable “track surfaces over time” in the surface wizard for nuclei segmentation.
Segment 10–50 time frames at a time by selecting them in the “region of interest” window.
Follow the segmentation wizard to the end.
Merge nuclei groups by selecting “merge” in the surfaces editing tab.
Select “tracking” in the “rebuild” tab to track nuclei through time after merging all nuclei.
Place spheres around transcription sites that encapsulate the full fluorescence for transcription site identification.
Identify nascent transcription foci using the MCP-GFP channel as “source channel”.
Specify the spot/sphere size in the next window.
Estimate transcription foci to be 1.8 μm in XY diameter.
Determine the “model PSF-elongation along z-axis” based on the microscope used and the dataset analyzed.
Place three-dimensional spheres of identical size around the transcription signal by the software.
Check that full fluorescence is contained within the sphere at time points where the fluorescent signal is brightest.
Adjust the sphere size if the full fluorescence is not contained within the sphere.
Use filters to classify spots, selecting Quality, Sum Intensity of MCP-GFP channel, Position Z, and Distance to image border XY for removing false-positive spots.
Identify real fluorescence spots by applying selected filters.
Check spots created by the software by navigating through time frames.
Verify that fluorescent signal is strong enough to detect transcription sites.
Identify and exclude false-positive spots if present.
Use Imaris X-Tension “XTSpotResizer” written by Egor Zindy to change spot sizes simultaneously.
Download XTSpotResizer files from https://github.com/zindy/Imaris.
Integrate downloaded files into Imaris under Edit -> Preferences -> Custom Tools.
Locate and add the folder containing XTSpotResizer files in the X-Tension folder field.
Add XTSpotResizer to custom tools in Imaris.
Use XTSpotResizer for resizing spot objects from the Image Processing menu.
Exclude transcription sites from nuclei on the edge of the field of view due to potential signal detection issues.
Remove inherent background fluorescence from unbound MCP-GFP using the sass.py script.
Fit a linear regression line based on background fluorescence values determined in this step.
Determine the average background fluorescence present at each time point using the line equation.
Subtract the average background fluorescence from the transcription site fluorescence measurements.
Manually add a second set of spots, of the same size as those used to identify transcription foci, to generate background readings.
Identify the first time frame that contains an MS2 signal.
Add “new spots” using the Imaris wizard by selecting “skip automatic creation, edit manually.”
Manually add 4 spots in the nuclear layer but outside of the expression domain or away from nuclei with active transcription.
Ensure the background spots have the same size as spots used to identify transcription foci.
Add 4 background spots in every third-fifth time frame until the end of the time-lapse movie.
Select the surface icon that contains the tracked nuclei.
Select the "statistics" tab and "detailed."
Export "all statistics to file."
Make sure the filename contains the word "cells."
Select the spots icon that contains the identified transcription sites.
Select the "statistics" tab and select "detailed."
Export "all statistics to file."
Make sure the filename contains the word "spots."
Select the spots icon that contains generated background spots.
In the "statistics" tab, select "detailed."
Export "all statistics to file."
Make sure the filename contains the word "background."
Create a specific folder structure for running the custom python script: parent folder -> subfolder containing Imaris statistics.
Manually note x-axis positions of boundaries that contain a group of similarly timed nuclei in the file “key_time.txt”.
Note down the time frame in which nuclei undergo telophase in column 3 of “key_time.txt”.
Download the custom python package “sass” from https://github.com/TMinchington/sass
Install Python 3 (or Anaconda3) on the computer.
Navigate to the folder containing the sass.py file using the Anaconda Prompt.
Type: python sass.py [drag and drop the parent folder containing the subfolder with the exported Imaris statistics]
Run the analysis.
Answer “n” if asked about creating a key time file during mitosis correction.
Inspect the quality of the analyzed data before continuing with downstream analysis.
Use the assignments.png file in the analysis folder as an indicator for successful nuclear tracking and spot identification.
Ensure that less than 5% of nuclear traces have more than 1 spot assigned to indicate successful processing.
If the value exceeds 5%, investigate potential false-positive spots or gaps in nuclear tracks.
Plot the mean fluorescence intensity and transcription onset time of all analyzed nuclei.
Visualize a few individual nuclear traces for comparison with other biological replicates.
